actor.note: This interim rule does not detect commands whose ancestry does not pass through readable processes of the same user to their agent, for example after reparenting or credential-changing helpers, nor a caller that replaces or instruments hgs itself or writes the team store directly. Agents started without session markers are also not detected. A command in a sandbox with its own user namespace is refused, so team commands must run outside such a sandbox. A DeepSeek session's command is proven by its host's per-call token instead of by ancestry, and only under a host that advertises those tokens; a host started before them is never restarted for it. A DeepSeek child agent's command is proven as its top-level session and acts with that session's standing, as an in-process Claude or Codex subagent does; a DeepSeek fork is its own session. One DeepSeek host process serves every session of its agent home: process ancestry proves only that this command runs under the host that serves the session, and the host's per-call token proves which conversation's tool call started it. The host socket's peer credentials prove that the answering socket is the recorded host's, which never hands its listener to a child, and everything that socket serves hides a live token printed whole; a call can always disclose its own token, split or encoded. A same-user process that reads another tool call's environment can copy that call's token; that is deliberate instrumentation and outside this proof.
